strengths: The paper addresses a well-motivated and clearly stated problem: pose-free, extrapolative novel view synthesis with jointly aligned image and geometry generation, a setting not well covered by prior feedforward or pose-embedding generative NVS methods.

Cross-modal attention instillation is an interesting and reasonably novel mechanism, with a compelling motivation (geometry completion is more deterministic than image inpainting) supported by attention-map visualizations (Fig. 3).

Comprehensive quantitative evaluation across multiple datasets (zero-shot DTU, RealEstate10K, Co3D) with consistent gains over relevant baselines (PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat, LucidDreamer, GenWarp) in extrapolative settings.

Reasonable ablation design: progressive component ablation (Table 3), qualitative ablations (Fig. 13), pointmap normalization ablation (Fig. 9), and analysis of generalization to more reference views than used in training (Table 4).
The proximity-based mesh conditioning and normal masking are sensible engineering contributions for handling noisy off-the-shelf geometry predictions.
weaknesses: Evaluation circularity concern: ground-truth geometry for both training supervision and evaluation is VGGT-predicted pseudo-GT rather than measured geometry. Geometry metrics (Abs.Rel, δ1.25 in Tables 4-5) therefore partly measure agreement with the same model used to construct the conditioning, which weakens claims of 'geometric accuracy', especially for inpainted (unobserved) regions where the 'GT' is itself a hallucination.

The manuscript is visibly unfinished: Table 5 is labeled 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled', the project page URL in the abstract is blank, and there are numerous typos and figure-label errors (e.g., 'Geomtry', 'valids', 'vlaues', 'towarding'; Fig. 6 cites DUSt3R as [26] and NoPoSplat as [28], which are wrong reference numbers).

Some key comparisons are qualitative only: LVSM (Fig. 7) and generative NVS methods (CAT3D, ReconFusion, Gen3C) have no quantitative comparison, so claims of state-of-the-art extrapolative performance versus the broader generative NVS literature are not fully substantiated.

Novelty is somewhat incremental: the framework combines many existing components (GenWarp-style pointmap conditioning and reference networks, Marigold-initialized geometry U-Net, VGGT geometry prediction, aggregated attention from prior work); the core new contribution is largely the attention-map replacement in Eq. (7), whose behavior at inference and failure modes are not thoroughly analyzed.

Several methodological details are under-specified or hand-wavy: the convex-hull definition of extrapolative viewpoints on SE(3) is informal; stochasticity of diffusion sampling (single vs. multiple samples, seed sensitivity) is not discussed for quantitative metrics; and how cross-modal attention instillation is applied during inference (when image and geometry denoising are coupled) could be clearer.
The 'MoAI' abbreviation is introduced in the abstract/figure but never consistently used in the method section ('distillation' vs. 'instillation' terminology is inconsistent).

PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS gains in extrapolative settings partly reflect that generated (hallucinated) content cannot match GT pixel-wise for any method; perceptual fidelity of generated content beyond metrics is only qualitatively shown.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem—joint novel view image and geometry synthesis from unposed sparse views—and the formulation of NVS as geometry-conditioned inpainting is a reasonable and well-motivated framework that enables extrapolative viewpoints beyond pose-embedded generative methods.

The proposed cross-modal attention instillation is a sensible mechanism for enforcing image–geometry alignment, and the observation that geometry completion is more deterministic than image inpainting is an interesting empirical insight.

Evaluation covers multiple datasets (DTU zero-shot, RealEstate10K, Co3D) with both interpolative and extrapolative protocols, and includes a component ablation and an analysis of varying the number of input reference views.
Qualitative results demonstrate plausible generation in occluded regions and robustness to noisy warped geometric conditions compared with naive warping-and-inpainting baselines.
weaknesses: The submission is not camera-ready: Table 5 is explicitly marked 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled', the project page URL in the abstract is empty ('available at .'), and there are numerous typos and errors ('Geomtry', 'valids', learning rate written as '1×10', 'in Fig. 12, conduct qualitative evaluation'). This draft-level polish is below the standard expected at a top-tier venue.

There is a circularity concern in the geometric supervision and evaluation: ground-truth geometry for training and evaluation is VGGT's own pseudo-ground-truth predictions, so geometry metrics largely measure consistency with VGGT rather than true geometric accuracy, weakening the central claim of accurate geometry synthesis.

Quantitative evaluation of geometry is only self-referential (Ours vs. their own baseline). There is no geometry comparison against any external method, and no comparison with strong generative NVS systems (e.g., CAT3D, ReconFusion, Gen3C) that the paper positions itself against; baseline comparisons are mostly against feedforward reconstructors, which are admittedly not generative and thus arguably unfairly evaluated under extrapolative settings.

The claimed contribution of cross-modal attention instillation is only weakly supported quantitatively: the ablation attributes a modest gain (PSNR 17.01→17.41) to it, and there is no ablation isolating whether attention instillation during inference alone, or the bidirectional synergy claim, is responsible; the 'synergistic multi-task' narrative is not rigorously verified.

Novelty is incremental: the framework is a fairly direct multi-view extension of existing warping-and-inpainting methods (GenWarp, LucidDreamer) with attention aggregation borrowed from prior work (e.g., Animate Anyone, GenWarp), and attention-map transfer is a known distillation technique.

Several technical details are under-specified or questionable: the formal 'convex hull in SE(3)' definition of extrapolative views is ad hoc; the claim that reference pointmap masks are always 1 assumes perfect off-the-shelf geometry; and the choice of Marigold's normal head as initialization for pointmap denoising is not ablated.

Missing statistics and protocol details: no error bars or multiple seeds, no inference cost/comparison, and the 'extrapolative view selection' custom protocol makes cross-paper comparison difficult and potentially favorable to the authors' method.
Reproducibility is limited: no code release is indicated, the project page is absent, and some implementation details contain errors, making independent verification difficult.

strengths: The paper addresses a meaningful and well-motivated gap: few-shot novel view synthesis with extrapolation capability from unposed references, while jointly producing aligned geometry — a combination that prior generative NVS methods (Zero-1-to-3, MVDream, CAT3D) and feedforward methods (PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat) do not offer.

The cross-modal attention instillation idea is sensible and well-argued: replacing spatial attention in the geometry U-Net with image U-Net attention creates a synergistic multi-task setup where deterministic geometry completion regularizes image generation, and the analysis of modality-dependent completion behavior (Fig. 3) provides an intuitive motivation.

The framing of novel view geometry synthesis as geometry completion/continuation of reference geometry elegantly sidesteps the scale-and-shift ambiguity of monocular depth prediction, which is a real and well-known failure mode.

Comprehensive experimental coverage: zero-shot evaluation on DTU, in-domain evaluation on RealEstate10K, both interpolative and extrapolative protocols, comparisons against feedforward, warping-and-inpainting, and LVSM baselines, plus component ablations and multi-viewpoint generalization tests.

The reported quantitative gains are substantial, particularly in extrapolative settings (e.g., PSNR 15.58 vs 14.66 for 2-view on DTU; 17.41 vs 14.36 on RealEstate10K), and the model generalizes to 3- and 4-view inputs without retraining.
The proximity-based mesh conditioning with normal masking is a practical, well-motivated solution for handling noisy point clouds from off-the-shelf geometry predictors.
weaknesses: Circularity in geometry supervision and evaluation: ground-truth geometry is pseudo-GT predicted by VGGT — the same model used for conditioning at inference. The paper's central claim of accurate, aligned geometry synthesis is thus evaluated against predictions of its own conditioning model rather than true 3D supervision (e.g., DTU laser scans), which weakens the evidence for the geometry claims considerably.

The manuscript is visibly incomplete: Table 5 is explicitly marked 'Incomplete, under experiment being filled', and the project page URL is blank in the abstract. This alone is disqualifying at submission time for a top-tier venue.

Novelty is somewhat incremental. The architecture is assembled almost entirely from existing components: GenWarp's pointmap correspondence conditioning, Animate Anyone-style reference networks and aggregated attention, Marigold initialization for the geometry U-Net, and VGGT for geometry prediction. The genuinely new element is attention-map sharing between two U-Nets, which is a relatively small architectural modification, and its individual contribution in the ablation is modest (17.01 -> 17.41 PSNR).

Missing key baselines for the joint image+geometry setting: there is no quantitative comparison against methods that could produce geometry (e.g., CAT3D/ReConfusion followed by reconstruction, or VGGT/MASt3R-based completion pipelines). Table 5 compares geometry accuracy only against the paper's own baseline, not against any external method.

The extrapolative evaluation protocol (sampling the furthest target cameras) structurally favors generative methods over reconstructive ones; PSNR in heavily occluded extrapolated regions mostly measures hallucination plausibility rather than reconstruction accuracy. A perceptual/3D-consistency evaluation or user study would be needed to substantiate the 'state-of-the-art extrapolation' claim, and none is provided.

The theoretical/definitional treatment of extrapolation in SE(3) (convex-hull of camera poses) is informal and imprecise; SE(3) is not a vector space, so convex combinations of pose matrices are not rigorously defined. This section reads as post-hoc justification rather than a principled protocol.

Reproducibility concerns: no code or weights release is stated, inference details (sampler, number of denoising steps, runtime, memory) are absent, and there are multiple errors undermining confidence (learning rate stated as '1x10', batch size 1 with unclear accumulation count, DTU cited as [34] which is RealEstate10K, 'Geomtry' typos, broken abstract link).

The multi-viewpoint analysis (Table 4) is performed on RealEstate10K only, and the single-view capability discussed in the appendix is not quantitatively evaluated, leaving the claimed scalability across view counts only partially supported.

Missing ablation on the key design choice of using image-branch attention as replacement (vs. addition, vs. feature-level distillation), and no analysis of failure cases or when cross-modal instillation could hurt (e.g., when image attention is itself wrong).

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation: quantitative results on RealEstate10K (in-domain), DTU (zero-shot), Co3D, plus comparisons to feedforward (PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat), warping-and-inpainting (LucidDreamer, GenWarp), and large model baselines (LVSM, ViewCrafter, ZeroNVS), covering both interpolative and extrapolative settings.

The proposed cross-modal attention instillation (sharing image U-Net attention (Q,K) with the geometry branch while keeping modality-specific values) is a sensible mechanism for image–geometry alignment, and is well motivated by the qualitative attention analysis in Fig. 3.

Thorough ablation study (Table 3, Fig. 15) isolating the contribution of each component, plus analyses on number of reference views, robustness to Gaussian perturbation and sparsity of the geometric condition (Tables 5-6), and a cross-predictor validation with DepthAnything v3 (Fig. 14).

The method addresses a practically meaningful gap: pose-free, generative NVS with explicit geometry output at arbitrary (including extrapolative >90°) viewpoints without per-scene optimization, at reasonable inference cost (~10s vs. hours for SDS-based methods).
Detailed implementation and training information in the appendix (initialization, schedulers, camera-space pointmap normalization with ablation), and a stated commitment to public code/weights.
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: the framework is largely an assembly of existing components—warping-and-inpainting from GenWarp/LucidDreamer, aggregated attention from Seo et al. (2024), reference networks from Animate Anyone, and Marigold-initialized geometry U-Nets. The main new piece (MoAI attention sharing) is a relatively simple architectural modification, so the contribution may be seen as incremental.

Circularity in geometry supervision: pseudo ground-truth for training and for geometry evaluation is generated by VGGT (the same class of model used at inference). This raises concerns about the reliability of the reported geometry metrics (Abs.Rel, δ1.25) and about training-inference distribution alignment; no evaluation against true 3D ground truth or an independent evaluator for the main geometry metrics is provided.

Evaluation protocol clarity: the 'extrapolative view selection' (furthest target cameras) and the definition of extrapolation (position outside convex hull, ignoring direction) may favor generative methods; details on number of test scenes, target-view sampling, and masking of unknown regions for PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS computation are insufficiently specified. Also, interpolative performance on DTU/RealEstate10K is sometimes below baselines (e.g., 24.23 vs. 25.03 PSNR for NoPoSplat), which softens the state-of-the-art claim.

No quantitative image–geometry alignment metric or multi-view consistency metric (e.g., cross-view reprojection error, FID/KID for generative quality) is reported; the alignment claim is supported mainly by qualitative visualizations.

Presentation quality issues that undermine polish: multiple typos ('Geomtry', 'In-domian', 'learning rate is set to 1×10', 'DoPoSplat'), incorrect citations (DTU referenced as Zhou et al. 2018, which is RealEstate10K; DTU is Jensen et al. 2014), and apparent inconsistencies between Table 1 and Table 4/ablation numbers (e.g., 15.58 vs. 17.41 vs. 20.08 PSNR for similar 2-view extrapolative settings without clear protocol differences explained).

Comparisons to 1-view warping baselines reuse the authors' choice of VGGT for those baselines; how sensitive LucidDreamer/GenWarp results are to this choice is not analyzed, and some ablation deltas (e.g., mesh conditioning +0.08 PSNR) are small relative to reported variance.

strengths: The overall system design—joint image and pointmap inpainting with a shared correspondence conditioning scheme—addresses a real limitation of prior warping-and-inpainting NVS methods (scale-shift discrepancy in depth completion), and the resulting colored point cloud completion output is a nice deliverable.

The proposed cross-modal attention instillation is well motivated by a complementary-attention analysis (Fig. 3) and avoids cross-modal feature mixing by sharing only structural attention, which is a defensible design decision.

The experimental section covers multiple settings (zero-shot DTU, in-domain RealEstate10K, single- and multi-view), includes component-wise ablations, robustness tests to noisy/sparse geometry conditions, inference-time comparisons against large models, and qualitative results on in-the-wild data, with a substantial appendix.
The paper is generally well organized and readable, and the authors commit to releasing code and weights.
weaknesses: The training and evaluation of geometry are fundamentally circular: ground-truth pointmaps for supervision are pseudo-labels produced by VGGT (the same off-the-shelf predictor used at inference), and the geometry metrics (Abs.Rel, delta) are computed against these pseudo-ground-truths rather than real GT. This weakens the central claim of 'aligned, accurate geometry'—the model largely learns to reproduce VGGT outputs, and reported geometry accuracy cannot be interpreted as true 3D accuracy.

Novelty is modest: the framework is a direct extension of existing warping-and-inpainting pipelines (LucidDreamer, GenWarp) with aggregated attention reused from prior work, and MoAI reduces to substituting attention maps from one fine-tuned U-Net with those of another. The empirical gains from MoAI in the ablation (PSNR 17.01 -> 17.41) are small relative to the claims of a 'synergistic multi-task' mechanism.

Baseline selection and fairness are questionable: quantitative comparisons against large-model baselines (CAT3D, ReconFusion) are missing entirely; ViewCrafter and LVSM appear only in a small appendix table on DTU, while the qualitative comparison (Fig. 7) uses differently resourced settings. The 'extrapolative view selection sampling the furthest target cameras' protocol is introduced by the authors without justification and may not be comparable to prior protocols.

Metric inconsistencies and reporting errors undermine confidence: ablation numbers (e.g., 15.58 vs 17.41 PSNR across tables) are not clearly tied to a single consistent protocol; the learning rate is reported as '1×10' (missing exponent); 'Referecne', 'In-domian', 'Geomtry', and 'weight W' (for width) appear repeatedly, suggesting insufficient proofreading.

The dependency on VGGT is critical but under-analyzed: since camera poses, pointmaps, and supervision all come from VGGT, failure cases where VGGT geometry or poses are wrong are only addressed with synthetic Gaussian perturbations and random masking, which do not reflect realistic correlated errors of geometry predictors.

Several important design questions are unaddressed: why attention-map sharing (Eq. 7) yields bidirectional synergy is asserted rather than demonstrated with controls (e.g., geometry->image-only instillation, feature-level conditioning alternative); the ball-pivoting mesh conversion is sensitive to noisy point clouds but no quantitative ablation of mesh vs. raw pointmap conditioning is isolated from the depth/normal augmentation.

Resolution (512x512) and batch-size-1 training details raise reproducibility and scalability questions, and the '9.67s' inference claim excludes the VGGT geometry prediction time that is required by the pipeline.

strengths: The paper addresses a practically relevant problem: pose-free, extrapolative novel view synthesis with jointly aligned image and geometry generation, which is not well served by existing feedforward (interpolation-limited) or pose-conditioned generative (in-domain pose limited) approaches.

The core idea — formulating NVS as geometry-guided inpainting of both image and pointmap, with cross-modal attention instillation (MoAI) so the geometry branch reuses the image branch's attention maps — is reasonably novel and well-motivated. The motivating analysis in Fig. 3 (complementary failure modes of image vs. geometry denoising) is a nice touch.

The proximity-based mesh conditioning (ball-pivoting mesh, depth/normal augmentation, normal masking) is a sensible engineering contribution that addresses a real failure mode of sparse, noisy off-the-shelf geometry predictions.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: zero-shot DTU, in-domain RealEstate10K, Co3D qualitative results, comparisons against feedforward baselines (PixelSplat, MVSplat, NoPoSplat), warping-and-inpainting methods (LucidDreamer, GenWarp), and large models (LVSM, ViewCrafter, ZeroNVS) with favorable inference time.

Good supporting analyses: component ablation, robustness to Gaussian perturbation and sparsity in the geometry condition, arbitrary number of reference views at inference, camera-space pointmap normalization ablation, and cross-predictor validation with DepthAnything v3.
Fair-comparison effort is visible (e.g., giving warping baselines the same VGGT geometry predictor), and the appendix covers training details, memory/latency, and LLM-usage disclosure.
weaknesses: Circularity in geometry supervision and evaluation: ground-truth geometry for training and for the geometry metrics (Abs.Rel, delta) is VGGT predictions on target images, not real GT. Claims of 'geometrically aligned point clouds' and geometry accuracy are therefore largely self-referential to the geometry predictor used for conditioning, weakening the significance of the geometry results.

The extrapolative-view quantitative protocol is author-defined (furthest target cameras, convex-hull criterion ignoring viewing direction), and PSNR/SSIM on fully hallucinated regions is a questionable fidelity measure — generative content that differs from GT is penalized, so the comparison to non-generative feedforward baselines under this protocol should be interpreted more cautiously than the paper does.

Novelty of MoAI is moderate: replacing/instilling attention maps between branches is a natural extension of existing multi-branch attention-sharing schemes (e.g., reference-net designs, GenWarp's correspondence signals, He et al. 2024), and the overall framework is a multi-view extension of LucidDreamer/GenWarp-style warping-and-inpainting. The ablation gain from MoAI itself is modest (~0.4 dB).

Some experimental inconsistencies and presentation errors undermine polish: DTU is cited as 'Zhou et al. (2018)' in Table 1 caption (it is Jensen et al., 2014); 'weight W' for width; 'In-domian'; the learning rate is reported as '1×10' (likely a typo); 1-view Ours beats 2-view Ours on the interpolative setting in Table 1 without explanation.

The 'synergistic multi-task' claim is asserted more than demonstrated: the paper shows the geometry branch benefits from image attention, but evidence that the image branch genuinely benefits from the coupling (vs. simply adding a geometry branch) is limited to qualitative Fig. 3 and a small ablation delta.

Heavy dependence on off-the-shelf VGGT quality; failure cases when VGGT geometry or poses are wrong are not systematically characterized beyond synthetic perturbation tests. Mesh conditioning via ball-pivoting on noisy sparse clouds may itself fail in unstructured scenes, and no runtime/memory cost of this step is reported.

Scalability of the aggregated attention with N reference views and dual U-Nets raises compute concerns; 28GB memory and dual-branch inference are non-trivial, and training details (batch size 1) suggest limited scalability, though this is acknowledged implicitly.
